The evidence suggests that Ent-Gloeosteretriol directly targets Mitogen-activated protein kinase kinase kinase kinase 3, which in turn is targeted by Sinocalycanchinensin G. This chain of targets ultimately leads to the activation of Homeodomain-interacting protein kinase 3. Additionally, Ent-Gloeosteretriol is also shown to target Caco-2, which is similarly targeted by Sinocalycanchinensin G, reinforcing the role of Sinocalycanchinensin G as a central mediator in the interaction. The integration of these pathways highlights a possible mechanism where Ent-Gloeosteretriol influences the signaling cascade through Sinocalycanchinensin G, ultimately affecting Homeodomain-interacting protein kinase 3. The evidence supports a direct or indirect relationship, with the central role of Sinocalycanchinensin G as a key mediator in the interaction between Ent-Gloeosteretriol and Homeodomain-interacting protein kinase 3.
